currentContext.business: OCCL is among a select group of global manufacturers with the capability to produce insoluble sulphur, a technically complex chemical used in tyre manufacturing and marketed under the premium brand Diamond Sulf; its products play a critical role in rubber vulcanisation, enhancing durability, heat resistance and performance stability. The Company supplies specialised chemical solutions to leading tyre and rubber manufacturers across global markets, with exports contributing 36% of revenue in FY26, and its products are marketed in 22 countries through a network of agents and strategically located warehouses. It also runs a sulphuric acid and oleum business, which the AR states delivered a strong performance in FY26 and supported overall profitability. The Company began in 1978 as Dharuhera Chemicals Limited producing sulphuric acid, entered insoluble sulphur in 1994, and today serves as the dedicated platform for the Group's chemical business, listed on BSE and NSE.

Insoluble Sulphur: High-performance insoluble sulphur grades for demanding tyre applications
Advanced insoluble sulphur grades under development through the Company's pilot plant

currentContext.expansion: OCCL's expansion history is presented as a milestones timeline rather than as a forward capex plan. The Company was incorporated in 1978 as Dharuhera Chemicals Limited and commenced sulphuric acid production; it merged with Oriental Carbon Limited in 1984 to form Oriental Carbon & Chemicals Limited; and it commissioned the insoluble sulphur manufacturing facility in 1994, entering a specialised chemical segment. The 2000-2011 block records the divestment of the carbon black business to sharpen focus on specialty chemicals, the initiation of a greenfield investment at Mundra to establish a new insoluble sulphur manufacturing facility, and the commissioning of the first phase of the Mundra plant with 5,500 MTPA capacity. The 2012-2018 block records the second phase of the Mundra plant with an additional 5,500 MTPA capacity (2012), the initiation of a brownfield expansion programme in Mundra (2016), and the commissioning of the first (2017) and second (2018) phases of the Mundra expansion. The 2019-2022 block records the initiation of an additional 11,000 MTPA brownfield expansion at Dharuhera (2019), the commissioning of a 5,500 MTPA expansion at Dharuhera (2021), and the commissioning of additional sulphuric acid capacity (2022). Separately, the timeline carries a milestone that the Company 'Doubled its insoluble sulphur capacity following the commissioning of a second production line at Dharuhera'. FORWARD-LOOKING CAPEX: the AR discloses no new named expansion project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. On the contrary, the Chairman states that prospective growth can be serviced substantially through existing capacities without correspondingly large capital expenditure, and the Operational review describes the recent programme as debottlenecking of capacities to extract higher throughput from existing assets, increasing the share of renewable energy in the energy mix, strengthening product development capabilities (including a pilot plant for future insoluble sulphur grades), and co-development with leading global customers. The Company also commissioned renewable power capacities that generate electricity at a lower cost, and holds an investment in associate Clean Max Infinia Private Limited, established to leverage the Government of Haryana's captive solar power generation scheme for its Dharuhera plant (that associate had not commenced operations during the financial year ending March 31, 2026). risks.risk: Chinese import dumping and duty absorption in the Indian insoluble sulphur market
risks.note: Chinese manufacturers, burdened by excess capacities, directed surplus volumes into the Indian market at aggressive prices. An anti-dumping duty of USD 307 per tonne was imposed, but Chinese exporters absorbed the duty by lowering their selling prices ('anti-absorption'), negating the benefit available to domestic manufacturers. The Company applied for and the DGTR has initiated an anti-absorption investigation, and a further anti-dumping duty absorption application was filed in March 2026; both outcomes are pending, so the distortion is unresolved. As India's leading domestic insoluble sulphur manufacturer, OCCL states it 'bore the brunt of this'. [PROVENANCE: this bundle carried only the boilerplate Directors' Report risk-management-policy paragraph; the substantive risk content is back-filled from the Directors' Report OPERATIONS and FUTURE PROSPECTS sections and the Chairman's statement, which were routed to the profile and strategy_outlook bundles.]

risks.risk: Sulphur raw-material cost inflation and supply concentration in the Gulf
risks.note: Average sulphur cost rose from Rs 29 per kg to Rs 52 per kg during the year, reflecting geopolitical disruptions across global supply chains. Ongoing Middle East tensions and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have curtailed sulphur availability and disrupted shipping routes and logistics; nearly 45-50% of global sulphur exports originate from Gulf countries, so the industry remains highly vulnerable, and this has resulted in an 80%-100% rise in prices of sulphur and oil. The Company is securing raw materials from various sources, even at a premium, and has raised inventory. [Back-filled from profile / strategy_outlook bundles.]

risks.risk: Margin compression - realisations cannot keep pace with input costs
risks.note: Sulphur prices remained elevated while pricing flexibility in the insoluble sulphur market stayed constrained amid intense global competition, so cost pressures moved faster than realisations across parts of the market. Insoluble sulphur realisations could not increase in proportion to the rise in input costs, resulting in margin compression; profitability in FY26 was supported by the sulphuric acid business rather than the flagship product. Energy, freight and insurance costs have also risen sharply and are expected to adversely impact the business. [Back-filled from profile / strategy_outlook bundles.]

risks.risk: Demand destruction from historically high input costs
risks.note: Management explicitly flags that 'the historically high input costs may result in demand destruction, which could negatively affect our sales volumes going forward'. Sales volume was already flat during FY26. [Back-filled from strategy_outlook bundle.]

risks.risk: Working capital intensity has roughly doubled
risks.note: 'In order to sustain business in this environment the Working Capital requirement has almost doubled.' Higher sulphur prices plus deliberately increased inventory levels lift capital employed and can offset the benefit of the Company's deleveraging, since the same disclosure sits alongside a stated shift to sourcing at a premium. [Back-filled from strategy_outlook bundle.]

risks.risk: Export concentration and geopolitical / trade-policy exposure
risks.note: Exports contributed 36% of revenue in FY26 and products are marketed in 22 countries. Export sales were adversely affected in FY26 by a weak global macro-economic and geopolitical environment, duties imposed by the USA, and the Iran-Israel war and its economic repercussions in the region. The Company states it had been absorbing part of the US tariff burden before the February 2026 tariff reduction. [Back-filled from profile / strategy_outlook bundles.]

risks.risk: Sulphuric acid demand risk from fertilizer-sector production cuts
risks.note: Elevated sulphur and other input prices are forcing fertilizer industries to cut production because the Government subsidy is not seen as enough to mitigate the cost increase, resulting in less demand for sulphuric acid. A subsidy revision is expected but not confirmed. This matters because the sulphuric acid and oleum business was the profit support in FY26 while insoluble sulphur margins compressed. [Back-filled from strategy_outlook bundle.]

risks.risk: Single-product / single-end-market concentration in tyre chemicals
risks.note: The Company's flagship product is insoluble sulphur sold principally into tyre manufacturing, and it describes itself as a dedicated platform for the Group's chemical business operating in one specialised global segment. The global insoluble sulphur market itself passed through 'one of its most testing phases in recent memory' driven by a sharp increase in global manufacturing capacities, muted tyre demand in select geographies and inventory overhangs across supply chains - a sector-wide overcapacity cycle to which the Company has no diversified offset beyond sulphuric acid. [Back-filled from profile bundle; stated as industry condition rather than under a 'Risks and Concerns' heading, which is absent from all six routed bundles.]

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

hero.oneLiner: OCCL Limited is a specialty chemicals manufacturer operating in the specialised global insoluble sulphur segment, supplying the tyre and rubber chemicals ecosystem under its premium Diamond Sulf brand, alongside a sulphuric acid and oleum business.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: OCCL Limited is a specialty chemicals manufacturer operating in the specialised global insoluble sulphur segment, supplying the tyre and rubber chemicals ecosystem under its premium Diamond Sulf brand, alongside a sulphuric acid and oleum business.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: OCCL is among a select group of global manufacturers with the capability to produce insoluble sulphur, a technically complex chemical used in tyre manufacturing and marketed under the premium brand Diamond Sulf; its products play a critical role in rubber vulcanisation, enhancing durability, heat resistance and performance stability. The Company supplies specialised chemical solutions to leading tyre and rubber manufacturers across global markets, with exports contributing 36% of revenue in FY26, and its products are marketed in 22 countries through a network of agents and strategically located warehouses. It also runs a sulphuric acid and oleum business, which the AR states delivered a strong performance in FY26 and supported overall profitability. The Company began in 1978 as Dharuhera Chemicals Limited producing sulphuric acid, entered insoluble sulphur in 1994, and today serves as the dedicated platform for the Group's chemical business, listed on BSE and NSE.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Insoluble sulphur market expected to remain highly volatile in 2026; Asia-Pacific continues to lead global demand, driven by robust manufacturing activity in China, India and South Korea
- India continues to be the fastest-growing market; GST rate cuts announced in September 2025 significantly boosted automobile sales, and April 2026 was the best-ever month for auto sales
- The reduction in US tariffs in February 2026 has positively impacted the Indian tyre industry and consequently OCCL's business; realisations are expected to improve as part of the tariff burden was previously being absorbed by the Company
- Supply-chain disruptions and rising sulphur prices have led Chinese manufacturers and other global suppliers to raise prices - previously a major obstacle to better realisations - and the Company was able to pass these increases on to customers and partially restore margins to sustainable levels, hence expects improved margins in FY 2026-27
- Demand from domestic tyre companies has seen an appreciable upturn in Q1 FY26-27 as import prices have increased and companies look to secure raw materials
- An anti-dumping duty absorption application filed with the DGTR for Chinese imports in March 2026, if implemented, is expected to further strengthen realisations
- Ongoing Middle East tensions and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have curtailed sulphur availability and disrupted shipping routes and logistics; nearly 45-50% of global sulphur exports originate from Gulf countries, leaving the industry highly vulnerable, and this has resulted in an 80%-100% rise in prices of sulphur and oil
- Energy, freight and insurance costs have risen sharply and are expected to adversely impact the business; working capital requirement has almost doubled to sustain business in this environment
- Historically high input costs may result in demand destruction, which could negatively affect sales volumes going forward
- Sulphuric acid: the Indian market is currently tight and bullish, driven by global sulphur shortages, with conditions more pronounced since March 2026 and a sharp increase in domestic prices; prices are expected to remain firm in the near term
- Sulphuric acid counter-driver: elevated sulphur and other input prices are forcing fertilizer industries to cut production because government subsidy is not seen as sufficient to mitigate the cost increase, reducing demand for sulphuric acid; the Government is looking into the matter and a revision is expected soon
- Structural demand driver cited from third-party sources: the global insoluble sulphur market was valued at USD 1.29 Billion in 2025 and is expected to reach USD 2.2 Billion by 2034, a CAGR of around 6.1%, with Asia Pacific accounting for over 56.25% of total demand
- Structural demand driver cited from third-party sources: shift toward premium and eco-friendly tyre formulations, with tyre OEMs adopting high-dispersion and low-oil (green) grades, and growth in EV-specific tyres
- Structural demand driver cited from third-party sources: India's replacement tyre segment accounted for nearly 58% of the total market in 2025, creating stable and recurring demand that insulates the industry when OEM vehicle sales slow

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: OCCL's expansion history is presented as a milestones timeline rather than as a forward capex plan. The Company was incorporated in 1978 as Dharuhera Chemicals Limited and commenced sulphuric acid production; it merged with Oriental Carbon Limited in 1984 to form Oriental Carbon & Chemicals Limited; and it commissioned the insoluble sulphur manufacturing facility in 1994, entering a specialised chemical segment. The 2000-2011 block records the divestment of the carbon black business to sharpen focus on specialty chemicals, the initiation of a greenfield investment at Mundra to establish a new insoluble sulphur manufacturing facility, and the commissioning of the first phase of the Mundra plant with 5,500 MTPA capacity. The 2012-2018 block records the second phase of the Mundra plant with an additional 5,500 MTPA capacity (2012), the initiation of a brownfield expansion programme in Mundra (2016), and the commissioning of the first (2017) and second (2018) phases of the Mundra expansion. The 2019-2022 block records the initiation of an additional 11,000 MTPA brownfield expansion at Dharuhera (2019), the commissioning of a 5,500 MTPA expansion at Dharuhera (2021), and the commissioning of additional sulphuric acid capacity (2022). Separately, the timeline carries a milestone that the Company 'Doubled its insoluble sulphur capacity following the commissioning of a second production line at Dharuhera'. FORWARD-LOOKING CAPEX: the AR discloses no new named expansion project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. On the contrary, the Chairman states that prospective growth can be serviced substantially through existing capacities without correspondingly large capital expenditure, and the Operational review describes the recent programme as debottlenecking of capacities to extract higher throughput from existing assets, increasing the share of renewable energy in the energy mix, strengthening product development capabilities (including a pilot plant for future insoluble sulphur grades), and co-development with leading global customers. The Company also commissioned renewable power capacities that generate electricity at a lower cost, and holds an investment in associate Clean Max Infinia Private Limited, established to leverage the Government of Haryana's captive solar power generation scheme for its Dharuhera plant (that associate had not commenced operations during the financial year ending March 31, 2026). [EXTRACTOR NOTES, recorded because the source is defective: (1) The milestone timeline is a graphic laid out as year-header rows followed by caption blocks, and the routed text preserves the blocks out of chronological order (1978/1984/1994, then 2019/2021/2022, then 2000/2005/2009/2011, then 2012/2016/2017/2018). The 2000/2005/2009/2011 header carries FOUR years but only THREE captions before the next header, with the 'Doubled its insoluble sulphur capacity ... second production line at Dharuhera' caption printed after the following header block under the label 'Milestones'. Its year is therefore NOT readable from the text and has not been assigned here. (2) The '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE - CAPITAL COMMITMENTS ===' block supplied in this bundle lacks readable column dates - its header line reads only '[page 74] Year Ended | As at' with no year against either column - so the two figures cannot be attributed to a period and have been OMITTED from capex_disclosed per the rule. The '=== MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION & ANALYSIS ===' heading delivers the Corporate Overview / Corporate Snapshot spread and truncates mid-sentence at 'The Company reported maintained an 18% EBITDA margin'. moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Technology / know-how barrier: OCCL is 'among a select group of global manufacturers with the capability to produce insoluble sulphur, a technically complex chemical', and among a select group able to produce high-performance grades for demanding tyre applications
- Cost position: the Company states it 'enjoyed the capability to manufacture insoluble sulphur at a cost lower than prevailing greenfield benchmarks', positioning it among the more competitive players globally within its scale of operations
- Brand: Diamond Sulf is described as widely recognised for quality, reliability and consistency; brand credibility rests on dependable supply and reliable delivery timelines
- Customer switching cost / approvals: the Company pursued increased customer plant approvals across geographies so multinational customers can source from OCCL for multiple manufacturing locations worldwide, deepening wallet share
- R&D and product development: continuous investment in process and product research; a pilot plant is used to develop future insoluble sulphur grades; co-development initiatives with leading global customers
- Manufacturing flexibility: demonstrated ability to customise product grades and production volumes in line with customer requirements
- Distribution reach: products marketed in 22 countries supported by agents and strategically located warehouses
- Balance-sheet resilience (qualitative): the Company states it prepaid debt, has 'virtually no long-term debt', and endured the downcycle without any operating loss, impaired Balance Sheet or loss in competitive position; it reported a profit in each of the last sixteen quarters
- Sustainability credentials as a commercial moat: Responsible Care and EcoVadis Gold cited as reinforcing customer confidence with global customers who evaluate suppliers on sustainability alignment
- Systems-driven organisation combining promoter leadership with professional management

strategy.body:

- Pass through raw-material and input-cost increases into selling prices to partially restore margins to sustainable levels
- Pursue trade remedies against Chinese import distortion: an anti-dumping duty absorption application was filed with the DGTR in March 2026, and an anti-absorption investigation has been initiated and is under review
- Strengthen the business structurally …
